speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you are experiencing sudden-onset vertigo; to help me determine the cause, how long has this dizziness been occurring?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The clinical presentation of sudden-onset rotational vertigo lasting approximately 3 minutes, occurring upon changing position (going to bed), accompanied by nausea but followed by a return to baseline, is classic for BPPV.
